set -euo pipefail; src=/workspace/clay-global-research-entity; dst=/workspace/entityos-crush-omega; branch=chatgpt-work/entityos-crush-omega-bootstrap-20260913; git -C "$src" fetch origin "$branch"; mkdir -p "$dst/docs/entityos"; git -C "$src" show FETCH_HEAD:research_entity/coordination/entityos_crush_seed/DONOR_LOCK_2026-09-13.json > "$dst/docs/entityos/DONOR_LOCK.json"; cat > "$dst/docs/entityos/PORTABLE_CORE.md" <<'EOF'
# EntityOS powered by Crush — portable OMEGA core

The product boundary is the Crush runtime, not a VM. Crush remains the stable portable shell for UI, CLI, tools, MCP, permissions, providers and session presentation. OMEGA lives below that surface and above model/tool execution.

Portable core: GRID10 competition and broadcast, TITAN MX state dynamics, Unified persistent state, LCME/dynamic cognitive compilation, GWT/reentry, identity, goals/hypotheses/world-model state, module competition and effect gating.

Hard boundary: the portable core must not require systemd, nspawn/VMs, Gabriel/Andreas paths, Local Bridge, browser/display, voice, or any specific model/provider. Models are interchangeable organs. A bundled 27B model is explicitly out of the core.

Current integration seam: `internal/omega.Runtime.Compile()` executes before model inference and produces a bounded deterministic cognitive frame; `Reenter()` receives the terminal outcome before Crush publishes run completion. A nil runtime maps to `NoopRuntime`, preserving upstream behavior.

Development law: on every explicit `CRUSH` trigger refresh the current live OMEGA donor, Gabriel's working Crush harness donor and this project before porting the strongest nonduplicate semantic delta. One writer per mutation boundary; parallel work is read-only or disjoint.
EOF
cd "$dst"; git add docs/entityos; git commit -m 'entityos: lock live donors and portable core boundary'; echo HEAD=$(git rev-parse HEAD); git log -2 --oneline; git status --short --branch
